questions.question: A train runs for 3 hours at the rate of 65 km/hr and for next two hours at the rate of 70 km/hr. Find the average speed of the train during 5 hours journey(in kmph).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The train runs for 3 hours at speed 65 kmph

Its speed increased to 70 kmph in next two hours

Formula used:

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

Calculation:

Total distance travelled in first 3 hrs = 65 × 3 = 195

Total distance in next 2 hrs = 70 × 2 = 140

Total distance of the journey = 140 + 195 = 335

Average speed = 335/5

⇒ Average speed = 67

**∴ Average speed to the train for the entire journey = 67 kmph**

questions.question: Raj’s income is Rs. 45,000 and his expenditure is Rs. 33,000. If his income is increased by 20% and expenditure by 12%, then what will be the percentage increase in saving?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Income : Expenditure : Savings = 45000 : 33000 : 12000 = 15 : 11 : 4

Using the weighted average method: Income = Expenditure + Savings

Let the percentage increase in savings be x%.

15 × 20% = 11 × 12% + 4 × x ⇒ 300% = 132% + 4x ⇒ 4x = 168% ⇒ x = 42%

**∴ The correct answer is 42%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹45,000

Initial Expenditure = ₹33,000

Income is increased by 20% and Expenditure is increased by 12%.

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase in Value ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a65412a82785a82ec15c9150c672853ca11c5292282400ba4b7b06e94055e4e2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Savings = ₹45,000 − ₹33,000 = ₹12,000

⇒ New Income = ₹45,000 + (20% of ₹45,000) = ₹45,000 + ₹9,000 = ₹54,000

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹33,000 + (12% of ₹33,000) = ₹33,000 + ₹3,960 = ₹36,960

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure

⇒ New Savings = ₹54,000 − ₹36,960 = ₹17,040

⇒ Increase in Savings = ₹17,040 − ₹12,000 = ₹5,040

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (5,040 ÷ 12,000) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = 42%

**∴ The correct answer is 42%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure Concept

Income is always the sum of Expenditure and Savings. Any absolute or percentage change in income naturally distributes across changes in both expenditure and savings.

Weighted Average (Alligation) Method

When a base quantity is divided into two parts, the net percentage change in the total is mathematically equivalent to the weighted average of the percentage changes in its individual parts: I × I% = E × E% + S × S%.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A positive result directly indicates an increase, while a negative result indicates a decrease.

questions.question: The traffic lights at 3 different road crossings change after every 48 sec, 72 sec and 108 sec respectively. If they all change simultaneously at 8:20 am, then what time they will again change simultaneously ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The lights will change simultaneously after an interval equal to the LCM of their individual times.

LCM of 48, 72, and 108 = 432 seconds.

Converting to minutes: 432 seconds = 7 minutes and 12 seconds.

Next simultaneous change = 8:20:00 am + 7 min 12 sec = 8:27:12 am.

**∴ The correct answer is 8:27:12 am.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Traffic light 1 interval = 48 sec

Traffic light 2 interval = 72 sec

Traffic light 3 interval = 108 sec

Time of first simultaneous change = 8:20:00 am

**Formula Used:**

Next simultaneous change = Initial time + LCM(t₁, t₂, t₃)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 48 = 2⁴ × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 72 = 2³ × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 108 = 2² × 3³

⇒ LCM(48, 72, 108) = 2⁴ × 3³

⇒ LCM = 16 × 27 = 432 seconds

⇒ Convert 432 seconds into minutes = 432 ÷ 60

⇒ 432 seconds = 7 minutes and 12 seconds

⇒ Adding this interval to the initial given time:

⇒ Next change time = 8:20:00 am + 00:07:12

⇒ Next change time = 8:27:12 am

**∴ The correct answer is 8:27:12 am.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest multiple that is exactly divisible by every member of a set of numbers. It is primarily used to determine when multiple periodic events will synchronize and happen together again.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest positive integer that divides all the given numbers without leaving a remainder. It is commonly used for dividing different quantities into the largest possible equal groups.

Relationship between LCM and HCF

For any two specific numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is strictly equal to the product of their LCM and HCF: a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b).

Fractions Rule for LCM

To calculate the exact LCM of multiple fractions, use the direct formula: LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between policemen and thief = 120 m

Speed of the thief = 7 km/h

Speed of policeman = 8 km/h

**Concept Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 8 – 7 = 1 km/h [they are running in the same direction]

⇒ 1 km/h = 1 × (5)/(18) = (5)/(18) m/s

⇒ Time taken to cover 120 m = (120)/(frac{5){18}} = (120 ×18)/(5) = 432 s

⇒ Speed of the thief = 7 km/h = 7 × (5)/(18) = (35)/(18) m/s

⇒ Distance covered by the thief in 432 s = (35)/(18) × 432 = 840 m

**Therefore, thief runs 840 m before he is caught by the policemen**

questions.question: Three men entered into a business in partnership for 14 months, 8 months and 7 months. If the ratio of their profit is 5 : 7 : 8, what is the ratio of their investments?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a partnership, Investment Ratio = Profit Ratio ÷ Time Ratio.

Given Profit Ratio = 5 : 7 : 8 and Time Ratio = 14 : 8 : 7.

Investment Ratio = 5/14 : 7/8 : 8/7

Multiply by LCM of denominators (56) to simplify.

Investment Ratio = (5/14 × 56) : (7/8 × 56) : (8/7 × 56) = 20 : 49 : 64

**∴ The correct answer is 20 : 49 : 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time period of investments (T₁ : T₂ : T₃) = 14 : 8 : 7

Ratio of profits (P₁ : P₂ : P₃) = 5 : 7 : 8

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Investment × Time ⇒ Investment = Profit ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d1c30c96888e099f29b2564221ed1215194cbf1f283379ce3a41d690159d468.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the investments be I₁, I₂, and I₃.

⇒ I₁ : I₂ : I₃ = (P₁ ÷ T₁) : (P₂ ÷ T₂) : (P₃ ÷ T₃)

⇒ I₁ : I₂ : I₃ = 5/14 : 7/8 : 8/7

⇒ To convert fractions to integers, multiply by the LCM of 14, 8, and 7, which is 56.

⇒ I₁ = 5/14 × 56 = 20

⇒ I₂ = 7/8 × 56 = 49

⇒ I₃ = 8/7 × 56 = 64

⇒ The ratio of their investments is 20 : 49 : 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 : 49 : 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Distribution Rule

The profit earned in a partnership is directly proportional to both the amount invested and the time period of the investment. P₁ : P₂ = (I₁ × T₁) : (I₂ × T₂).

Active Partner

A partner who takes part in managing the business is called an active or working partner. They often receive a fixed salary or a certain percentage of total profit before the remaining profit is divided according to investment ratios.

Sleeping Partner

A partner who only invests capital but does not participate in the daily operations of the business is known as a sleeping or dormant partner. Their return is solely based on their capital and time invested.

__
 
• **Kala-azar**, also known as visceral leishmaniasis, is caused by the protozoan parasite **Leishmania donovani**.
 
• The disease is transmitted to humans through the bite of infected female **phlebotomine sandflies**.
 
• **Symptoms** of Kala-azar include prolonged fever, weight loss, enlargement of the spleen and liver, and anemia.
 
• It primarily affects people in **tropical and subtropical regions**, including countries like India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Brazil, and Sudan.
 
• Without treatment, Kala-azar can be fatal, but it is treatable with antileishmanial drugs such as **Amphotericin B** and **Miltefosine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leishmaniasis**

 
 
• Leishmaniasis is a disease caused by infection with Leishmania parasites, which are spread by the bite of infected sandflies.
 
• There are three main forms of leishmaniasis: visceral (Kala-azar), cutaneous, and mucocutaneous.
 
• Cutaneous leishmaniasis causes skin sores, while mucocutaneous leishmaniasis can lead to ulcers in the mouth, nose, and throat.
 
 
 
• **Phlebotomine Sandflies**
 
 
• These are the vectors responsible for transmitting Leishmania parasites to humans.
 
• They are tiny, about one-third the size of mosquitoes, and are typically active during dusk and dawn.
 
 
 
• **Diagnosis and Treatment**
 
 
• Diagnosis of Kala-azar often involves serological tests, bone marrow or spleen aspiration, and PCR testing.
 
• Treatment includes antileishmanial medications such as Amphotericin B, Miltefosine, and Sodium Stibogluconate.
 
 
 
• **Prevention**
 
 
• Preventive measures include vector control through insecticide spraying, use of bed nets, and reducing exposure to sandfly bites.
 
• Education and awareness campaigns are crucial in endemic areas to prevent the spread of the disease.

• National income serves as a key indicator for measuring the economic performance of a country.

• GDP is the monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.
 
• It is the most commonly used metric to assess a country's economic health.
 
• GDP can be calculated using three approaches: **Production, Income, and Expenditure**.
 
 
 
• **Central Statistical Organisation (CSO):**

questions.question: In India which of the following concepts is not used for calculating unemployment?

__
 
• The three main measures used for calculating unemployment in India are **Usual Status Unemployment, Weekly Status Unemployment,** and **Daily Status Unemployment.**
 
• **Usual status unemployment** refers to the activity status of a person over a longer reference period, typically a year.
 
• **Weekly status unemployment** identifies individuals who were unable to find work for at least one hour during the reference week.
 
• **Daily status unemployment** captures the activity status of individuals on each day of the reference week.
 
• **Annual status unemployment** is not a recognized or standard concept used by the Government of India for calculating unemployment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Unemployment is measured by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** is the official source for unemployment data in India, introduced in 2017-18.
 
• Unemployment is broadly classified into **open unemployment, disguised unemployment, structural unemployment, and cyclical unemployment.**
 
 
 
• **Usual Principal Status (UPS):**
 
 
• This approach determines the activity status of a person over a longer reference period, typically 365 days preceding the date of the survey.
 
• An individual is considered unemployed if they were not engaged in any economic activity for the major part of the year.
 
 
 
• **Current Weekly Status (CWS):**
 
 
• In this approach, the reference period is the last 7 days preceding the survey.
 
• A person is considered unemployed if they did not work for at least 1 hour on any day during the reference week.
 
 
 
• **Daily Status Unemployment:**
 
 
• Daily status measures unemployment on a day-to-day basis.
 
• This approach provides a detailed and dynamic understanding of employment fluctuations.
